units: metres; rest offsets are in the PARENT bone's local frame; rotations in clips are Euler XYZ degrees applied in the bone's local frame
axes: right-handed, +X right, +Y up, +Z forward. yaw 0 faces +Z, matching the existing controller (pos[0] += sin(yaw)*d, pos[2] += cos(yaw)*d).
chest_node_note: the node RI-CMB06 §A/§B's line-of-sight ray, aim point and vertical framing are measured against

hurtbox_axes._note: Each hurtbox capsule runs from its parent bone's ORIGIN along the given local axis for the length declared in hitgeometry.json. That makes 'the capsule follows the bone' literal: the capsule's segment IS a segment of the bone, so RI-CMB04 M1's 'distance from the capsule axis midpoint to its declared parent bone origin' is exactly length/2 on every frame of every pose, which is the invariance M1 checks.

weapon.blade_axis_note: The blade runs along the grip hand's local -Y, so at the identity rest pose the weapon hangs point-down from a lowered hand — the readable 'weapon at rest' silhouette in every reference still. Every clip rotates the hand and forearm to raise, cock and swing it.

wpn_guard._note: at the guard, one grip-length down the blade axis from the hand

weapon.socket_rule: socket_world = hand_world_position + hand_world_rotation * (blade_axis_local * (grip_offset_m + t * capsule_length_m)). capsule_length_m comes from hitgeometry.json per class; grip_offset_m is 0.10 for every class.

standing_collider._note: the MOVEMENT capsule. It is NOT the hurtbox — reusing it as one is RI-CMB04 'How we lose' #5.
